newsitem.title: USA: Allstate up after Q3 beats expectations.
newsitem.headline: Allstate up after Q3 beats expectations.

text.p: Shares of Allstate Corp rose more than five percent after the big personal lines insurer reported better-than-expected third quarter earnings.
The earnings, which included a large charge to strengthen loss reserves, declined compared to a year ago.

But the underlying results showed surprising strength in the company's auto and life insurance businesses, analysts said. Allstate reported third quarter operating earnings of $0.58 a share compared to $0.90 a year ago. Wall Street's consensus estimate was $0.47 a share.
Excluding the various special items, Allstate's third quarter operating income was $1.14 a share.
Allstate shares rose 3-1/2, or more than six percent, to 54-7/8 in mid-afternoon trading.
"I thought it was a terrific quarter for them," said Alex Brown analyst John Hall. Hall said he estimated third quarter earnings, excluding the special items, at $1.04 a share.
Allstate's better-than-expected results followed surprising good earnings from Progressive Corp on Wednesday. Both companies are major personal auto insurers.
Progressive shares rose two, or over three percent on Thursday, to 63 in mid-afternoon on Thursday after closing up 5-3/8 on Wednesday.
Other smaller auto insurers also are likely to report solid third quarter results following the strong performances from Allstate and Progressive, analysts said.
Integon Corp, which is expected to report earnings next week, rose 1-1/8 to 20 and Mercury General Corp MCY.N rose 1-1/4 to 51.
However, Integon last month said third quarter results will be hurt by losses stemming from hurricanes Fran and Bertha.
Auto insurers are benefiting as older and wiser drivers get behind the wheels of safer cars, equipped with air bags and other life-saving technology, said Conning & Co analyst Gary Ransom.
But insurers like Allstate and Progressive also are reaping gains as they redesign their claims processing management.
Allstate, for instance, began implementing a new claims resolution process at the end of 1994 and expanded it nationwide throughout 1995, Allstate president Edward Liddy said.
The new process seeks to resolve claims quickly and without lawyers in order to keep the process less costly.
"The bigger companies are putting more effort into claims reengineering," Ransom said.
And by handling claims more effectively, they can lower their costs and offer their products to customers at more attractive prices, he said.
Ransom said he would expect to see Progressive and Allstate compete more aggressively on price in coming months.
